posts.title: Why Korean Kids Start Taekwondo at Six
posts.material: cotton belt, gift of the dojang
posts.summary: The taekwondo bus stops outside the apartment at 3:10. It is yellow, it is loud, and it is the highlight of Raon's day.
text: The taekwondo bus stops outside the apartment at 3:10. It is yellow, it is loud, and it is the highlight of Raon's day.
In Korea most kids start around six, partly for the discipline and partly because the dojang bus solves the after-school problem.
Raon learned to bow, to count to ten in Korean at full volume, and to tie his own belt, which took a week and about four hundred attempts. The belt is white. It is already turning gray.

posts.title: A Rainy Saturday at the National Museum of Korea
posts.summary: 비 오는 토요일, 역사의 길을 따라 걷다 사유의 방에서 멈춘 이야기.
text: It rained the way Seoul rains in September, sideways. We took Line 4 to Ichon and walked the covered path to the museum. Raon counted seventeen umbrellas before we reached the door.

Inside, the Path to History was quieter than we expected. We went straight up to the Room of Quiet Contemplation while it was still empty and stood there for about four minutes, which for a seven-year-old is a very long time. He asked why the Buddha was half-smiling. We said nobody has told him the answer yet either.
Then we came down and found the celadon. Raon asked whether the fish on the vase were real. We said yes. He accepted this, and we left for kalguksu at 12:40, wet and pleased.

Tips for families: go on a Wednesday or Saturday evening if you can, when it is open late and quieter. Start with the Room of Quiet Contemplation before the queue forms. The children's museum needs a reservation.

posts.title: Han River Picnic with a Seven-Year-Old
posts.summary: A mat, kimbap, and the first time Raon rode a bicycle without the little wheels. It happened on the grass by Ichon Hanga
text: A mat, kimbap, and the first time Raon rode a bicycle without the little wheels. It happened on the grass by Ichon Hangang Park at about four in the afternoon, after two falls and one dramatic lie-down.
Shun ran alongside for the first ten meters and then he was gone, wobbling toward the river with the confidence of someone who has not yet learned about brakes.
We had pizza afterward, because that is what you do after a first bicycle ride.

posts.title: Kalguksu After the Museum
posts.summary: There is a kalguksu place two streets from Ichon station that we have now been to three times, always in the rain. The b
text: There is a kalguksu place two streets from Ichon station that we have now been to three times, always in the rain. The broth is anchovy and something else the owner will not tell us.
Raon eats the noodles first and leaves the clams for Dad, which Dad considers a fair trade. This time he also ate the kimchi, which is new.
We paid, put our hoods up, and walked back to the station arguing about whether the museum or the noodles were the best part. The noodles won, two to one.

posts.title: Dad's 10,000 Steps Challenge
posts.summary: Thirty-one days, ten thousand steps each, a 51-year-old salesman. The museum visit turned out to be eleven thousand on i
text: Thirty-one days, ten thousand steps each, a 51-year-old salesman. The museum visit turned out to be eleven thousand on its own.
What I learned: the steps are easy, the shoes are not. Buy the shoes first.

posts.title: Messi Meets the Museum Cat Plushie
posts.summary: We brought home a small cat plushie from the museum shop. Messi, our actual cat, regarded it for a full minute from the
text: We brought home a small cat plushie from the museum shop. Messi, our actual cat, regarded it for a full minute from the top of the bookshelf, then came down, sniffed it twice, and sat on it.
This is, we think, approval. The plushie now lives under the sofa, where Messi keeps things she has decided are hers. Raon wanted it back. Negotiations are ongoing.
